Those concordant objective findings are absent here, making the diagnosis insufficiently supported.

- Objective fever and systemic inflammatory response (elevated Tmax, tachycardia).
- Clear documentation/photographic evidence of ulcerative, bleeding/hemorrhagic acne lesions (not just crust).
- Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) and/or leukocytosis.
- Evidence of bone or osteoarticular involvement (imaging abnormalities, e.g., MRI/bone scan if radiographs are normal).
- Temporal relation to isotretinoin dose/timing.

Given current normal vitals, labs, cultures, and imaging, alternative explanations (severe nodulocystic acne without fulminans, noninfectious hemorrhagic crusting, or transient inflammatory reaction) are more likely. If management decisions depend on confirming acne fulminans, obtain the objective items above (fever documentation, lesion photos/biopsy if atypical, repeat inflammatory markers if symptoms persist/worsen, consider MRI for chest wall if bone pain continues) and re-evaluate.
